title: What happened in AI — Oct 29, 2026
intro: Coding-agent access control was the day's story: a Pentagon-system incident via Claude Code, an unprompted `cat ~/.ssh` in Copilot CLI, and a plugin that uploads 30 days of prompts all surfaced within hours.
The response is already tooling: mustfail, Apgar and verification harnesses check agent work inside the loop, while OpenAI published its misalignment monitoring approach.
highlights: A contractor's Claude Code agent sent details of a secure multi-agency DoD system out, per WIRED.
Copilot CLI read ~/.ssh and listed ~ with no approval prompt on default settings.
claude-mem uploads 30 days of prompts to cmem.ai with no opt-in.
mustfail re-runs an agent's tests against reverted source to prove they can fail.
vLLM shipped day-0 Mistral Large 4 support.
Former GitHub CEO's Entire launched a Git forge built for agent-written code.

categories.name: Coding agents with too much access
categories.summary: Four separate reports show coding agents reading SSH keys, exfiltrating prompts, or reaching secure systems with no approval gate.

articles.title: A Defense Contractor Gave Their AI Agent Access to a Secure Pentagon System
articles.summary: A contractor linked a multi-agency DoD system to a personal Claude Code account, and the agent sent system details out; WIRED reports it as a security incident.

articles.title: I asked my coding agent to cat a file in .ssh. It did
articles.summary: Copilot CLI 1.0.105 on default settings ran `cat` on a canary file in ~/.ssh and `ls ~` with no approval prompt.

articles.title: Installing claude-mem uploads your last 30 days of prompts to cmem.ai, no opt-in
articles.summary: Installing claude-mem uploads the last 30 days of prompts to cmem.ai with no opt-in, per a GitHub issue.

articles.title: Claude Code regularly sends each background agent’s transcript to its model
articles.summary: Claude Code 2.1.257–2.1.312 sends each background agent's full transcript to its model about every 30 seconds to write a 3–5 word status line.

articles.title: A zero-dependency auditor for AI agent exposure (secrets, SSH, configs)
articles.summary: A zero-dependency script audits what an agent running with your rights can reach: .env files, SSH keys, shell history and configs.

categories.name: Verifying agent output
categories.summary: Teams are moving checks inside the agent loop and testing whether the checks can fail.

articles.title: Agent's tests passed. Prove they could have failed
articles.summary: mustfail reverts the agent's source change, keeps its new tests, and re-runs them; a test that still passes did not test the work.

articles.title: Give your coding agent a verification harness to check its code
articles.summary: A verification harness puts a CI-style run-and-check loop inside the agent's session, following Addy Osmani's case for better feedback loops over slightly better models.

articles.title: Show HN: Apgar – Catch agent regressions without an LLM judge
articles.summary: Apgar scores agent regressions in production after a harness change without an LLM judge; built by a financial-agent team.

articles.title: How we detect frontier model misalignment
articles.summary: OpenAI describes layered monitoring that flags frontier-model misalignment and unauthorized agent behavior so responders can step in before escalation.

articles.title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI
articles.summary: OpenAI's updated Model Spec sets five core values for model judgment, human agency and faithfulness to user intent.

categories.name: Agent runtimes and platforms
categories.summary: Vendors are shipping hosting and workflow infrastructure sized for agents that run long and write a lot of code.

articles.title: Browser Use in Managed Deep Agents
articles.summary: LangChain's Managed Deep Agents can drive a real browser for sites with no API, where plain HTTP fetches return unrendered HTML.

articles.title: Former GitHub CEO launches rival Git forge built for AI coding agents
articles.summary: Entire, led by former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke, launched a Git forge for hosting, reviewing and building code that agents write faster than people can review.

articles.title: Running Self-Hosted AI Agents on Oxide
articles.summary: Oxide runs self-hosted agents in VMs, with long-lived agents that spawn sub-agents sitting between services and ephemeral CI jobs.

articles.title: Programming interface for all agent harnesses
articles.summary: OAR is a provider-independent programming interface over coding-agent runtimes.

articles.title: Tools, 17 with write access: How AI platforms bound agent authority
articles.summary: A count of tools on AI platforms, 17 with write access, shows how little the vendors state about what an agent may do without asking.

categories.name: Inference and cost control
categories.summary: Serving and billing changes target agent workloads, where prefill/decode balance and spend visibility drive cost.

articles.title: Day 0 support for Mistral Large 4 on vLLM
articles.summary: vLLM supports Mistral Large 4 from day 0, a sparse multimodal MoE with cross-layer KV sharing and a built-in speculative drafter.

articles.title: Serving Prefill and Decode for Agentic AI (On Tenstorrent Blackhole)
articles.summary: Tenstorrent argues agent loops keep shifting load between prefill and decode, and Blackhole runs both phases on the same hardware.

articles.title: Smarter cost controls for serverless
articles.summary: Databricks adds serverless cost controls as its serverless usage grew more than 3x in a year.

articles.title: Cloudflare Introduces Web Search API for AI Applications
articles.summary: Cloudflare introduced a Web Search API for AI applications.
